status: frozen before any settlement-model result; blind pools reserved here before development
question: An Earth-calibrated model of the atlas's unmarked settlements: where the towns (county seats, market and administrative centres) not marked on the map sit, how many there are and how they are spaced.
model: polity.settle.place_towns (greedy best-site-first placement with E1-fitted catchment spacing and the dry-land water rule) with the site score s = density^a x (1 + w_r exp(-water_km / 3)) x (1 + w_c [coast <= 6 km]) x (1 + w_d [road <= 4 km]) x 1 / (1 + k_f slope); current weights a 1, w_r 1, w_c 0.5, w_d 0.5, k_f 20 are assumptions; the count and spacing rule stay as E1 fitted them.
earth_runs: Earth windows of scripts/polity_earth_check.py (9 km): density = the Earth land/people density, water_km = distance to Natural Earth rivers, roads = Itiner-e AD 150 in the Rome window and none elsewhere, aridity from the window's WorldClim; no marked towns; allowed = the polity's extent where the pool has one, else all land.

development.rome_150: Hanson towns AD 150 in the Rome window, allowed = Cliopatria Roman Empire 150 (seen)
development.han_2: Han AD 2 county seats in the Han window, allowed = Han commanderies (seen)
development.hellenistic: Pleiades Hellenistic settlements in the B1 window (spent blind control pool, explicit development use)

blind.S1_sui_610: CHGIS V6 county seats alive in AD 610 (Sui) in the Han window, allowed = Cliopatria 'Sui Dynasty' 610 if present else the seats' convex land region; never used in this project
blind.S2_beyond_limes_1300: Bosker, Buringh & van Zanden (2013) cities present in 1300 (doi:10.7910/DVN/24747, cities.tab sha256 2b0df0f4...0bb5003e) in the Rome window north of 45 N, west of 30 E and outside Cliopatria's Roman Empire AD 150: towns of the medieval north beyond the old frontier, never used in this project

metrics.M1: Spearman rank correlation of real and predicted town counts per 100 km block (blocks with >= 30 % allowed land)
metrics.M2: matched placement: the model places exactly as many towns as the pool has; recall = share of real towns within 25 km (~1 day) of a placed town, precision = share of placed towns within 25 km of a real one, F1 their harmonic mean
metrics.M3: Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance between nearest-neighbour spacings of real and placed towns
metrics.M4: count error |log10(model count / real count)| with the model's own E1 count rule
metrics.M5: site-rank AUC for partial networks (S2, large cities only): site score at city cells against all allowed land cells

development_fit: Grid over a in {0.5, 1, 1.5}, w_r in {0, 1, 3}, w_c in {0, 0.5, 1.5}, w_d in {0, 0.5, 1.5}, k_f in {0, 20, 60} on the three development pools; candidate = the setting with the best mean M2 F1, subject to mean M1 not below the current weights'.

blind_gates.G1: candidate M2 F1 >= current-weights F1 on S1
blind_gates.G2: candidate M5 AUC >= current-weights AUC on S2
blind_gates.G3: candidate M1 on S1 not more than 0.02 below current
blind_gates.adopt: if G1, G2 and G3 pass, the fitted weights replace the assumptions in polity.settle and the atlases' unmarked towns are regenerated; else the current weights stay and the model is labelled 'count and spacing Earth-fitted, sites assumed'

data_status: Development pools are seen; S1 shares the Han window and many seat places with Han AD 2 (declared dependence); S2 is a new region (central and northern Europe beyond the Roman frontier) and era.
development_result_1: Grid (output/settlement_model_20261107/grid.json): current weights mean F1 0.453, M1 0.274; best a 1.5, w_r 3, w_c 0, w_d 1.5, k_f 60: F1 0.463, M1 0.288. Diagnosis: placed towns form a regular lattice (nearest-neighbour median 45 km, 10-90 % 37-57) while real towns cluster (median 20 km, 9-64): M3 KS 0.68-0.93. The E1 count is right (Han 1,303 vs 1,264).

amendment_1.status: before any blind outcome (the blind pools are unopened)
amendment_1.change: Development stage 2: count-limited placement. The model keeps its E1 count N (the towns the current spacing rule places) but places them greedily best-site-first with a smaller minimum spacing factor s (blocking radius s x R instead of 1.6 R), so towns crowd into the best land and poor land stays empty, as real networks do.
amendment_1.grid: s in {0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.3, 1.6 (current)} x site weights {current, stage-1 candidate}
amendment_1.selection: best mean F1 subject to mean M1 not below the current model's; M3 reported
amendment_1.gates_added: G4: candidate M3 (spacing KS) on S1 not above the current model's.

development_result_2: Count-limited spacing grid (grid2.json): smaller spacing fixes the spacing distribution (M3 0.80 -> 0.38-0.42 at s 0.4-0.6) but lowers F1 (0.46 -> 0.23-0.31) and M1, because the crowded towns follow the density field, which correlates weakly with real towns per block (Rome 0.28, Han 0.15). Candidate stays s 1.6 with stage-1 weights (F1 0.463, M1 0.289).

amendment_2.change: Development stage 3: site suitability fitted directly. Logistic regression of real-town presence (town cells against a random sample of allowed land, case-control) on map-derivable fields only: log(1 + food density), river proximity at 3 and 15 km, coast within 6 km, coast proximity at 30 km, elevation, slope, elevation relative to its 50 km mean, log aridity, road within 4 km; one intercept per pool. Site score = exp(linear predictor without the intercepts); placement keeps the E1 count and the 1.6 spacing.
amendment_2.validation: leave-one-pool-out: fit on two development pools, place and score on the third; the stage-3 candidate is the fit on all three pools, adopted for the blind test only if its leave-one-pool-out mean F1 beats the stage-1 candidate's in-sample mean F1 (0.463) and mean M1 is not below the current model's (0.274).
amendment_2.gates: unchanged G1-G4 on the blind pools, against the current model
